questions.text: Referral Pathway Integration: Connection to physical care: (1) Directory of physical facilities; (2) Electronic referral letters; (3) Feedback loop (did patient arrive?); (4) Emergency transport integration (ambulance/taxi); (5) Agreement with receiving facilities; (6) Continuity of care record transfer.
questions.evidence_required: Referral SOPs, MOUs with facilities, Referral tracking data
questions.africa_specific_notes: Telemedicine without referral is dangerous. 'Closed loop' referrals (knowing patient arrived) is the gold standard.

questions.text: Public Health Reporting (Surveillance): Disease tracking: (1) Auto-reporting of notifiable diseases (Cholera, Measles, Ebola); (2) Integration with DHIS2 (District Health Information System); (3) Anonymized population health dashboards; (4) Outbreak alert generation; (5) Compliance with MoH reporting mandates.
questions.evidence_required: DHIS2 integration logs, Reporting protocols, MoH acknowledgment
questions.africa_specific_notes: Private sector often fails to report outbreaks. DHIS2 is the standard for MoH data in Africa.

questions.text: Laboratory & Diagnostic Ecosystem: Connection to labs: (1) E-ordering of lab tests; (2) Sample collection logistics (riders); (3) Digital result delivery; (4) Quality assurance of partner labs; (5) Integration with lab information systems (LIS).
questions.evidence_required: Lab integration APIs, Partner lab QA reports
questions.africa_specific_notes: Diagnostics often missing link. 'Uber for labs' models growing.

questions.text: Health Insurance Integration: Who pays: (1) Integration with National Health Insurance (NHIF/NHIS); (2) Private insurer integration; (3) Real-time eligibility checks; (4) Digital claims submission; (5) Co-pay collection via mobile money; (6) Fraud detection in claims.
questions.evidence_required: Insurance API docs, Claims logs, Fraud detection rules
questions.africa_specific_notes: Out-of-pocket payment is a barrier. NHIF integration is the holy grail for scale. Claims fraud is rampant.

questions.text: Digital Payment Ecosystem: Mobile money for health: (1) M-Pesa/Mobile Money integration; (2) Installment plans for expensive care (health loans); (3) Voucher systems (donor funded); (4) Wallet system for savings; (5) Transparent receipts.
questions.evidence_required: Payment gateway logs, Loan product terms, Voucher redemption logs
questions.africa_specific_notes: Health wallets/savings help resilience. Vouchers common for maternal health programs.

questions.text: National Digital Health Strategy Alignment: Strategic fit: (1) Alignment with MoH eHealth strategy; (2) Adoption of national standards (HL7/FHIR); (3) Participation in technical working groups; (4) Interoperability with national health exchange.
questions.africa_specific_notes: Fragmented pilots ('pilotitis') plague Africa. Solutions must align with national strategy to scale.

questions.text: Cross-Border Regulatory Compliance: Regional expansion: (1) Compliance with regional blocks (EAC, ECOWAS); (2) Cross-border data transfer rules; (3) Mutual recognition of medical licenses; (4) Harmonized drug regulations.
questions.africa_specific_notes: Telemedicine crosses borders easily; regulation doesn't. Harmonization is slow.

questions.text: Community Trust & Acceptance: Social license: (1) Engagement with community leaders/chiefs; (2) Perception of digital vs traditional healers; (3) Trust in CHWs; (4) Stigma management (privacy trust); (5) Feedback mechanisms.
questions.africa_specific_notes: Traditional healers are the competition. Tech must complement, not alienate. Privacy trust is fragile.

questions.text: Gender Dynamics in Health Access: Women's access: (1) Female CHW availability; (2) Privacy for reproductive health; (3) Male involvement strategies; (4) Phone ownership gap (women borrowing phones); (5) GBV (Gender Based Violence) screening/referral.
questions.africa_specific_notes: Women often need husband's permission to seek care. Shared phones compromise privacy. GBV is a shadow pandemic.

questions.text: Language & Cultural Appropriateness: Cultural fit: (1) Local language support (beyond English/French); (2) Culturally relevant content (diet, lifestyle); (3) Respectful terminology; (4) Religious considerations.
questions.africa_specific_notes: Dietary advice must match local food. Religious views on contraception/vaccines matter.

questions.text: Power & Connectivity Resilience: Infrastructure reliance: (1) Solar power for clinics/devices; (2) Backup connectivity (dual SIM); (3) Offline-first architecture; (4) Paper backup processes.
questions.africa_specific_notes: Clinics often have no power. Solar is standard. Network outages are daily events.

questions.text: Medical Waste Management: Environmental impact: (1) Sharps disposal; (2) E-waste (old tablets/phones); (3) Expired drug disposal; (4) Incinerator access.
questions.africa_specific_notes: Digital health generates e-waste. Home care generates medical waste. Safe disposal needed.

scoring_notes: Layer 6 (Ecosystem) for Healthcare in SSA: Integration with the public sector (MoH) and insurance (NHIF) is the path to scale. Community trust and gender dynamics determine uptake.
